payload.name: Morphological-Expansion-For-Event-Counts
payload.description: When a question asks to count or enumerate all memories of an action or event, expand the action verb to its morphological variants and synonyms (e.g., win/won/wins/winning) and continue searching until a search returns no new relevant memories.
content: If the question asks for a count or full enumeration of events involving an action verb (e.g., 'how many games has John mentioned winning'), do not rely only on the exact keyword form. Search with morphological variants and synonyms of the verb (win, won, winning, wins, beat, victory) using keyword and semantic/hybrid strategies.

Before answering, verify recall: run one more expanded search if the latest search returned previously unseen memories that match the action; stop when a search returns no new relevant memories, then compute the count from all uniquely retrieved matching memories.

solves: The general failure is that exact-keyword search misses morphological variants of the action verb, causing undercounting when a question requires enumerating all matching event memories. This Skill applies when a future question asks how many or enumerate all instances of an action/event, where all relevant memories must be collected. It must not apply to single-fact lookup questions that are answered by one explicit match, where variant expansion is unnecessary.
